metadata.title: Next Role Readiness - Strategic Readiness Quick Diagnostic

opening_content.title: What's Really Blocking Your Next Role?
opening_content.introduction:
You've mastered the technical side. You deliver results. You lead teams.

So why aren't you in that strategic role yet?

This 12-question diagnostic reveals your Strategic Readiness Zone and the specific gaps between where you are and where you need to be for your next role.

Most senior IT leaders discover they're closer than they think—but stuck on 2-3 specific capabilities they didn't know were holding them back.
opening_content.value_proposition: What you'll discover: Your readiness zone, your biggest gaps, and your next move.

sections.section_description: How you think about and position your role
How you're perceived by executive stakeholders

questions.text: When presenting to C-suite executives, I typically:

options.label: Focus on technical architecture and implementation details
Report project status, timelines, and resource needs
Highlight capabilities delivered and technical achievements
Lead with business outcomes, ROI, and strategic impact
Frame technology initiatives as enablers of enterprise growth and competitive advantage

questions.text: I can explain my organization's business model (customer segments, value proposition, revenue streams, competitive advantage) without looking at slides:

options.label: Cannot do this / Would struggle significantly
Could provide a basic technical description
Can do it with some preparation and prompting
Can do it fairly well with business context
Can do it fluently, connecting technology decisions to business impact

questions.text: When faced with a business challenge, my first instinct is to:

options.label: Jump to technical solutions and tools
Analyze technical requirements and constraints
Ask about business context and stakeholder needs
Frame it as a strategic opportunity with trade-offs
Consider enterprise implications, competitive dynamics, and system-level impact

questions.text: In the past quarter, I have been actively consulted by business leaders (Sales, Marketing, Operations, Finance) on strategic initiatives unrelated to IT infrastructure:

options.label: Never / Not that I'm aware of
Once, for technical input
2-3 times, occasionally
4-6 times, fairly regularly
7+ times, I'm seen as a strategic business partner
Focus on technical architecture, tools, and infrastructure decisions
Describe technical capabilities and implementation roadmaps
Connect technology choices to departmental objectives
Frame technology in terms of business capabilities and market positioning
Articulate how technology creates competitive advantage and enables strategic business moves

questions.text: C-suite executives in my organization would most likely describe me as:

options.label: The person who keeps our systems running reliably
A solid technical leader who delivers IT projects
Someone who understands both technology and business needs
A business-minded technology leader who thinks strategically
A strategic partner who drives business transformation through technology

questions.text: In the last 3 months, I have been invited to contribute to (select the HIGHEST level that applies):

options.label: Technical architecture discussions within IT
IT strategy and roadmap planning
Cross-functional project and initiative planning
Business unit strategy sessions
Enterprise strategy, board discussions, or CEO-level strategic planning

questions.text: When I speak in executive meetings, the response is typically:

options.label: Polite listening, then conversation moves on
Questions about technical details or clarifications
Engagement with my points, some discussion
Executives lean in and ask follow-up questions about my strategic perspective
My input visibly shapes the direction of the conversation and decisions

questions.text: I have authentic, trusted relationships with:

options.label: My direct team members and immediate IT colleagues
IT peers and key technical stakeholders across the organization
Some business leaders in functions I regularly work with
Multiple C-suite executives beyond the CIO/CTO
Board members, CEO, and external strategic partners

questions.text: In the last month, how many C-suite executives (OUTSIDE of CIO/CTO) have you had a substantive conversation with that went beyond project updates or technical requests?

options.label: Zero
One
Two
Three to four
Five or more

questions.text: When organizational politics emerge around priorities or resources, I:

options.label: Try to stay out of it and focus on delivering my work
Get frustrated by the dynamics and wish people were more logical
Navigate them when absolutely necessary
Proactively anticipate and manage political dynamics
Strategically build coalitions, shape narratives, and influence outcomes

questions.text: In major organizational decisions that impact technology direction, I am:

options.label: Informed after decisions have been made
Asked for technical input or feasibility assessment
Consulted on IT-related aspects during planning
Actively involved in strategic planning and trade-off discussions
A key influencer who shapes the decision before it's made

scoring_logic.calculation: Sum all question values (q1 through q12)

priority_determination.logic: Identify the 2 dimensions with the lowest percentage scores

ZONE_1.title: Technical Expert
ZONE_1.current_reality: You're operating primarily as a high-level technologist. You deliver exceptional technical results, but you're largely invisible at the strategic table.
ZONE_1.gap: Significant distance to strategic leader identity. You're solving technical problems while others are shaping business direction.
ZONE_1.meaning: You're highly competent, but positioned wrong. The organization sees you as an implementer, not a strategist.

priorities.title: Strategic Business Thinking
priorities.description: Learn to speak the language of business value, not technical features

priorities.title: Executive Relationships
priorities.description: Build authentic connections with C-suite leaders outside IT

ZONE_1.next_step: Take the Complete Next Role Readiness Assessment to identify your specific breakthrough capabilities.

ZONE_2.title: Emerging Strategist
ZONE_2.current_reality: You're transitioning from technical expert to strategic contributor, but your positioning is inconsistent. Sometimes you're at the strategic table, sometimes you're not.
ZONE_2.gap: Moderate distance. You think strategically, but you're not consistently visible or influential at the executive level.
ZONE_2.meaning: You're on the cusp of breakthrough. 2-3 specific capabilities are holding you back from being seen as a strategic leader.

priorities.title: Strategic Communication
priorities.description: Translate every technical initiative into compelling business narratives

priorities.title: Cross-Functional Influence
priorities.description: Build credibility beyond IT as a business partner

ZONE_2.next_step: Join the 'Next Role Readiness' workshop to learn the exact frameworks that close these gaps.

ZONE_3.title: Strategic Contributor
ZONE_3.current_reality: You're recognized as strategic within your function, but not yet at the enterprise level. You influence IT decisions, but not business direction.
ZONE_3.gap: Final positioning and visibility barriers. You have the strategic thinking, but lack the organizational positioning.
ZONE_3.meaning: You're ready for a strategic role, but you're not positioned for it. The gap is visibility, relationships, and political capital.

priorities.title: Executive Presence
priorities.description: Position yourself as an enterprise leader, not just an IT leader

priorities.title: Political Capital
priorities.description: Build strategic influence across the C-suite

ZONE_3.next_step: Book a Next Role Roadmap Session to create your personalized positioning strategy.

ZONE_4.title: Executive Ready
ZONE_4.current_reality: You think strategically, communicate effectively, and have strong executive relationships. You're ready for a strategic or C-suite role.
ZONE_4.gap: Minimal. This is about timing, opportunity, and final positioning.
ZONE_4.meaning: You're not blocked by capability—you're blocked by opportunity visibility or organizational timing.

priorities.title: Strategic Opportunity Creation
priorities.description: Actively position yourself for the specific role you want

priorities.title: Personal Brand Amplification
priorities.description: Ensure decision-makers see your strategic value

ZONE_4.next_step: Book a strategy session to accelerate your timeline and position for specific opportunities.

cta_content.header: You've Discovered Your Zone. Now What?
cta_content.subheader: This quick diagnostic revealed your Strategic Readiness Zone and your top 2 priority areas.
cta_content.gap_statement: But here's what it DIDN'T reveal:
missing_insights: The *specific* behavioral gaps holding you back
How you compare to colleagues who've been promoted
Your detailed development roadmap with concrete actions
The precise frameworks that will close your gaps
cta_content.options_header: Three Ways to Accelerate Your Breakthrough:

options.title: Take the Complete Assessment
benefits: Detailed Gap Profile across all 6 dimensions
Specific frameworks mapped to your gaps

options.title: Join 'Next Role Readiness' Workshop
benefits: Learn the 3 frameworks that transform technical experts into strategic leaders
Live diagnostic discussion and gap analysis

options.title: Join Strategic Leadership Community
benefits: Weekly frameworks that build strategic presence
Peer learning with senior IT leaders in transition

consultation_cta.text: Or book a complimentary 15-minute consultation to discuss your results:

Strategic Business Thinking.description: The ability to understand and articulate business models, speak in terms of business value (ROI, competitive advantage, market positioning), and connect technical decisions to enterprise outcomes.
development_focus: Learn to explain your organization's business model fluently
Practice translating technical initiatives into business value stories
Study strategic frameworks like Business Model Canvas

Executive Relationships.description: Building authentic, trusted relationships with C-suite executives and business leaders outside of IT, positioning yourself as a strategic partner rather than a service provider.
development_focus: Schedule regular 1-on-1s with business leaders
Understand C-suite priorities and pain points
Practice executive-level communication

Strategic Communication.description: The ability to translate complex technical concepts into compelling business narratives that resonate with non-technical stakeholders and inspire action.
development_focus: Lead with business outcomes in all presentations
Master the art of strategic storytelling
Develop executive presence in communication

Cross-Functional Influence.description: Building credibility and influence across the organization beyond IT, being consulted on strategic initiatives, and shaping decisions outside your functional area.
development_focus: Volunteer for cross-functional strategic initiatives
Build relationships with peers in Sales, Marketing, Operations, Finance
Position yourself as a business partner, not just a technical resource

Executive Presence.description: How you show up in executive settings—your gravitas, confidence, strategic thinking, and ability to command attention and respect at the highest levels.
development_focus: Master executive communication techniques
Develop strategic thinking frameworks
Build your personal brand as a strategic leader

Political Capital.description: Your ability to navigate organizational politics, build coalitions, anticipate and manage resistance, and shape narratives to influence strategic outcomes.
development_focus: Map the informal power structure in your organization
Practice building strategic coalitions
Learn to anticipate and address political dynamics

Strategic Opportunity Creation.description: Proactively identifying and positioning yourself for specific strategic roles, creating visibility for your capabilities, and accelerating your promotion timeline.
development_focus: Define your target role clearly
Build relationships with decision-makers
Create opportunities to demonstrate strategic value

Personal Brand Amplification.description: Ensuring that decision-makers consistently see and recognize your strategic value, positioning yourself as an indispensable strategic asset to the organization.
development_focus: Share strategic insights regularly
Speak at high-visibility forums
Build thought leadership in your domain

for_developer.database_seeding: Use the 'questions' array to seed your Question model. Each question should include the section, order, text, and options. The 'zones' object should seed your Zone/Interpretation model.
for_developer.frontend_rendering: Map the questions array to your React components. Use the 'order' field to sequence questions. Display one question at a time with radio buttons for options.
for_developer.scoring_implementation: Follow the 'scoring_logic' object exactly. Calculate dimension scores first, then determine zone based on total score using 'zone_determination' ranges.
for_developer.results_display: After scoring, fetch the appropriate zone from 'zones' object using the zone_id. Display the zone title, current_reality, gap, meaning, priorities, and next_step.
for_developer.priority_calculation: Calculate percentage scores for each dimension (score / max_score * 100). Sort dimensions by percentage ascending. The two lowest become priority1 and priority2. Map dimension IDs to priority names using 'priority_determination.dimension_mapping'.
for_developer.cta_rendering: Use 'cta_content' object to display the call-to-action section on results page. Include header, missing_insights list, and all three options with benefits.

validation_rules.question_responses: All 12 questions must be answered. Each response must be an integer between 1 and 5 inclusive.
validation_rules.score_calculation: Total score must be between 12 and 60. Each dimension score must be between 4 and 20.
validation_rules.zone_assignment: Zone must be one of: ZONE_1, ZONE_2, ZONE_3, ZONE_4. Verify score falls within zone's min_score and max_score range.

api_endpoints.get_questions: GET /api/assessment/questions - Returns questions array in order
api_endpoints.submit_assessment: POST /api/assessment/submit - Accepts responses object {q1: 3, q2: 4, ...}, calculates scores, determines zone, saves to database, returns complete results
api_endpoints.get_results: GET /api/assessment/:id/results - Returns zone interpretation, priorities, dimension breakdown, CTA content
